details: The US Commerce Department has implemented new rules further restricting China's access to advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips from companies like Nvidia, including measures to block Chinese firms from renting these high-end processors abroad. In response, China's Commerce Ministry expressed "strong dissatisfaction and firm opposition," warning that it would take countermeasures if the US proceeds with the new restrictions. This escalation intensifies the ongoing tech war between the two global powers, potentially unsettling global chip supply chains and impacting technology-heavy equity markets.
title: US Imposes New AI Chip Curbs on China, Beijing Vows Countermeasures

details: The cryptocurrency market has entered a six-week downturn, with Bitcoin and Ethereum experiencing significant declines. Bitcoin fell 14% and Ethereum 18% in the week of November 9, with the broader crypto market losing 13% and closing at $2.2 trillion. Experts attribute this sustained selloff to tightening global liquidity, persistent geopolitical risks—particularly the ongoing conflict in the Middle East—and hawkish expectations from the Federal Reserve regarding future interest rate hikes. Concerns over global inflation and the prospect of higher borrowing costs continue to dampen investor risk appetite.
title: Geopolitical Risks and Hawkish Fed Fuel Crypto Market Selloff

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has issued a warning that the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence into debt finance is exhibiting "historical parallels with the dotcom and subprime bubbles." In its latest Financial Stability Review, the ECB estimated that major technology firms hold over $4 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments, raising concerns about excessive borrowing, risky investments, and a lack of transparency within the burgeoning AI sector.
title: ECB Warns AI Boom Shows Parallels to Dotcom and Subprime Bubbles

details: Russian President Vladimir Putin, speaking at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen, emphasized that Asia's developing economies have made a "giant leap forward" over recent decades. He noted their emergence as leaders of global development and innovation, profoundly impacting the global economy and world order. Putin highlighted that the Asia-Pacific region demonstrates how a more democratic and equitable world order is taking shape.
title: Putin Highlights Asia's "Giant Leap Forward" in Global Economy
